overview: Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer in women globally, with around 660 000 new cases and around 350 000 deaths in 2022. It is largely preventable through HPV vaccination and regular screening, and it can be cured if detected early and treated promptly. The highest rates of cervical cancer incidence and mortality are in low- and middle-income countries.
diagnosis: Cervical screening with a high-performance test
Self-collection of a sample for HPV testing
transmission: Sexual contact with an infected person
Skin-to-skin contact with an infected person
prevention: Cervical screening from the age of 30
Early detection of women with symptoms
Being a non-smoker or stopping smoking
key_facts: 660 000 new cases of cervical cancer in 2022
90% of girls fully vaccinated with HPV vaccine by age 15
70% of women screened by ages 35 and 45
90% of women with pre-cancer or invasive cancer receiving appropriate treatment
